title: Country-dance transportation and Bunk Johnson
summary: After Allen mentions Henry Allen's band in the photo, Williams talks about getting to country dances and the school dances, and says he heard Bunk Johnson's music around the Third and Fourth Wards as a boy.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Over 20 years ago you did that. I can see it's Henry Allen's Brown. Henry Allen's band with Brown and Nelson we were talking about, and Happy as Grand Marshal. Did you have much trouble with transportation, getting one place in another when you played those

country dances? One time the food burned up on me. I had about a car, a food that burned up. It burned up on me one time. And I used to call them, they just relayed, transferred us, and got us down there because we was very busy down there in Dayvan. Dayvan where we played that 25 cents dance down there and built that school up down there.
Oh, you were going on the bunk. Did you know him back when you were growing up or did you

know him in Lake? No, I had no bunk. I had no bunk when I was a boy. And then I lost track a bunk, bunk left here. I used to listen to his music up here in the Third Ward, Fourth Ward. He was all around here you know. He played around the battlefield and stuff?
